did_you_know.text: Did you know? The LORD commanded Jeremiah to buy a clay jar and bring along the elders of the people and the elders of the priests, so that they would witness the prophecy.
Did you know? Jeremiah was sent to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, near the entrance of the Potsherd Gate, where he was commanded to proclaim the LORD’s words.
Did you know? The prophecy is addressed to the kings of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, warning of a great disaster that will horrify everyone who hears about it.
Did you know? The sins mentioned in the chapter include abandoning the LORD, worshiping other gods, defiling the place, and shedding innocent blood.
Did you know? The chapter condemns burning sons as offerings to Baal and emphasizes that this was not commanded, spoken of, or even conceived by the LORD.
Did you know? The LORD declares that the Valley of Ben-hinnom and Topheth will no longer be called by those names, but instead the Valley of Slaughter.
Did you know? Jerusalem and its inhabitants will be struck down by the sword at the hands of their enemies, and their bodies will be given as food to the birds of the sky and the wild animals.
Did you know? The chapter’s description of the siege includes extreme hunger and distress, to the point of eating the flesh of sons, daughters, and one another.
Did you know? Breaking the clay jar in front of those accompanying him is a symbolic act: just as the jar is broken and cannot be repaired, so the city and the people will be shattered.

Did you know? After delivering the prophecy at Topheth, Jeremiah returned to the courtyard of the LORD’s Temple and continued proclaiming before the people the disaster that would befall Jerusalem and its cities.
